# FLUX 3 edit box by box

**Workflow:** [`flux3/flux3-box-edit.json`](../flux3/flux3-box-edit.json)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | `flux3` |
| Nodes | 11 |
| Links | 9 |
| Paid API calls per run | **1** |

---

Edit an image by its element table: each row says where an element is now and where it should end up, so the model knows what to keep, what to move, what to make new and what to take out.

| kind | effect |
| --- | --- |
| **keep** | anchored where it is |
| **move** | from its box to the `to_` box |
| **new** | generates `desc` in the box — adds, replaces, recolours |
| **remove** | erased; the model fills in what was behind it |

`ref_image` **0** is the first reference (`<ref_image_0>`); 1 is the second. Boxes are **[top, left, bottom, right]** on the 0–1000 grid of that image.

Say it twice: state every move, addition and removal in the instruction *and* in the rows. Add a **keep** row for anything that must not move — unlisted areas usually hold, anchors make it explicit. Name shadows and reflections in a removal so they go too.

No table for your image yet? Run **flux3-edit** once and copy the rows FLUX 3 wrote into `expanded_prompt`, then paste them into Layout Prompt's `rows_json`.

`variation` is not sent to the API — flux-3-image has no seed. It is **fixed** here so a rerun with nothing changed costs nothing; bump it (or set it to *randomize*) for a fresh take. `expanded_prompt` is `result.prompt`, the prompt the model actually used after expanding yours.

## The prompt lives in one node

The **Shared Prompt** node feeds the prompt in this graph, so there is one
place to edit it. It emits a plain string, **not** a list. That is the difference between it and **Prompt
List**, which would make each node it feeds run once per line and multiply what the graph
costs.
